mainTopic: Endings of ברכות in the עשרת ימי תשובה, teachings of רב on prayer and shame, which פרשיות belong in קריאת שמע, and mentioning יציאת מצרים at night
overview: The amud opens by finishing the topic of bowing in תפלה: רב ששת bowed all at once and rose up slowly. Next, רב rules that during the עשרת ימי תשובה we end two ברכות with הַמֶּלֶךְ הַקָּדוֹשׁ and הַמֶּלֶךְ הַמִּשְׁפָּט. רבי אלעזר says the regular wording is still valid, and the הלכה follows רבה, who sides with רב. Further teachings of רב follow. Whoever can pray for another person and does not is called a sinner. For a תלמיד חכם, a person must even make himself sick with worry. Whoever is ashamed of a sin is forgiven for all his sins, and this is proven from שאול המלך. The גמרא then returns to קריאת שמע. It explains why פרשת בלק was not added and why פרשת ציצית was. A new משנה rules that יציאת מצרים is mentioned at night, based on בן זומא's דרשה, and the חכמים disagree. The גמרא begins their debate about the days of the משיח, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: How רב ששת bowed and stood up
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת bowed down all at once, like a stick, and straightened up slowly, like a snake.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת: when he bowed, he bowed like a stick. When he stood up straight, he stood up like a snake.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells us how רב ששת personally bowed in שמונה עשרה. This closes the earlier discussion about the right way to bow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He bowed quickly in one motion, the way a stiff stick tips over. He came back up slowly, head first, the way a snake raises itself. The slow rising showed that he felt awe before הקב״ה and did not want to look like he was eager to be done with the bowing.

keyTerms.meaning: like a stick or cane, all at once
like a snake, slowly, head first

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet, when he bowed —
he bowed like a stick (all at once).
When he would straighten up —
he straightened up like a snake (slowly).
phrases.notes: A snake lifts its head first and then the rest of its body, slowly.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב שֵׁשֶׁת, כִּי כָּרַע — כָּרַע כְּחִיזְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues and closes the earlier discussion (on the previous amud) of how to bow in תפלה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Bow down in one quick motion, and rise slowly and respectfully.

steps.title: During the עשרת ימי תשובה we say 'the holy King' and 'the King of justice'
steps.stepSummary: רב rules that during the ten days from ראש השנה to יום כפור, the endings הָאֵל הַקָּדוֹשׁ and מֶלֶךְ אוֹהֵב צְדָקָה וּמִשְׁפָּט are changed to הַמֶּלֶךְ הַקָּדוֹשׁ and הַמֶּלֶךְ הַמִּשְׁפָּט.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבה בר חיננא סבא said in the name of רב: All year long a person prays 'the holy God' and 'King who loves righteousness and justice.' The exception is the ten days between ראש השנה and יום הכפורים, when he prays 'the holy King' and 'the King of justice.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new statement from the same רבה בר חיננא סבא. He reports רב's rule that two ברכה endings change during the עשרת ימי תשובה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All year we end the third ברכה with הָאֵל הַקָּדוֹשׁ, and the ברכה of השיבה שופטינו with מֶלֶךְ אוֹהֵב צְדָקָה וּמִשְׁפָּט. During the ten days of judgment we stress that הקב״ה is the King who sits in judgment. So we say הַמֶּלֶךְ הַקָּדוֹשׁ and הַמֶּלֶךְ הַמִּשְׁפָּט instead.

keyTerms.meaning: the holy God (the regular ending of the third ברכה)
the holy King (the ending used during the Ten Days)
the King of judgment, the King who shows Himself through judgment

steps.confusionAlert: The word וְאָמַר ('and he said') does not mean this statement continues the bowing topic. It is simply a second statement from the same speaker, רבה בר חיננא סבא, who was quoted earlier about bowing. Here he moves on to a new subject.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַבָּה בַּר חִינָּנָא סָבָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב
phrases.english: And Rabba bar Ḥinnana Sava said in the name of Rav:
All year long a person prays (concluding with)
'the holy God' and 'King who loves righteousness and justice,'
except for the ten days
between Rosh HaShana and Yom Kippur,
when he prays 'the holy King' and 'the King of justice.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבָּה בַּר חִינָּנָא סָבָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic from the same speaker who was quoted earlier about bowing.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: During the עשרת ימי תשובה, one ends these ברכות with הַמֶּלֶךְ הַקָּדוֹשׁ and הַמֶּלֶךְ הַמִּשְׁפָּט.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: saying 'the holy God' is still valid
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר holds that even if a person said הָאֵל הַקָּדוֹשׁ during the ten days, he has fulfilled his obligation.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אלעזר said: Even if he said 'the holy God,' he has fulfilled his obligation.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר disagrees with רב. He says that keeping the regular year-round wording during the ten days is still acceptable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב treated the change to הַמֶּלֶךְ as necessary. רבי אלעזר says the regular wording also works, so a person who said it is יצא. The disagreement is only about whether the change is required. Both agree the ten days are a special time of judgment.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Elazar said:
Even if he said 'the holy God,' he has fulfilled his obligation.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אָמַר אֲפִילּוּ אָמַר ״הָאֵל הַקָּדוֹשׁ״ — יָצָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רב's requirement from the previous step.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Saying הָאֵל הַקָּדוֹשׁ during the ten days still fulfills the obligation.

steps.title: Proof from ישעיה: the verse about judgment still says 'the holy God'
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר proves his view from ישעיה ה:טז. The פסוק speaks about the time of judgment, the ten days, and still uses the words הָאֵל הַקָּדוֹשׁ.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: 'And the Lord of Hosts is exalted through justice, and the holy God is sanctified through righteousness.' When is 'the Lord of Hosts exalted through justice'? These are the ten days from ראש השנה until יום הכפורים. And yet the verse says 'the holy God.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר brings a פסוק to support his ruling. He shows that even a verse about the days of judgment calls הקב״ה הָאֵל הַקָּדוֹשׁ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first half of the פסוק, 'exalted through justice,' describes the ten days of judgment. The very same פסוק then says הָאֵל הַקָּדוֹשׁ, not הַמֶּלֶךְ הַקָּדוֹשׁ. So the regular phrase already fits the ten days, and changing it is not required.

keyTerms.meaning: as it is said (introduces a פסוק)

phrases.english: As it is said: 'And the Lord of Hosts is exalted through justice,
and the holy God is sanctified through righteousness.'
phrases.notes: ישעיה ה:טז

phrases.english: When is 'the Lord of Hosts exalted through justice'?
These are the ten days
from Rosh HaShana until Yom Kippur,
and yet it says 'the holy God.'

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וַיִּגְבַּה ה׳ צְבָאוֹת בַּמִּשְׁפָּט וְהָאֵל הַקָּדוֹשׁ נִקְדָּשׁ בִּצְדָקָה״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the scriptural basis for רבי אלעזר's ruling.
steps.raayaObject: רבי אלעזר's view that saying הָאֵל הַקָּדוֹשׁ during the ten days is valid.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ישעיה ה:טז, which is read as describing the ten days of judgment and still uses הָאֵל הַקָּדוֹשׁ.

steps.title: What is the final ruling?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which view is accepted as the final הלכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What was concluded about this?
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא asks how the debate between רב and רבי אלעזר was decided, and the answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two opinions have been laid out, and each has its own reasoning. The question מאי הוה עלה asks for the practical ruling: must a person repeat the ברכה if he did not say הַמֶּלֶךְ?

keyTerms.meaning: what was concluded about it? (asking for the final ruling)

steps.whyThisMatters: The answer decides whether someone who forgot to say הַמֶּלֶךְ הַקָּדוֹשׁ has to go back and repeat, which is a well-known practical הלכה.

phrases.english: What was concluded about it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After both opinions are presented, the גמרא asks for the final decision.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the הלכה follows רב (one must say הַמֶּלֶךְ) or רבי אלעזר (הָאֵל הַקָּדוֹשׁ is also valid).

steps.title: רב יוסף keeps the regular endings
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף rules that the regular endings הָאֵל הַקָּדוֹשׁ and מֶלֶךְ אוֹהֵב צְדָקָה וּמִשְׁפָּט are said, following רבי אלעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: We say 'The holy God' and 'King Who loves righteousness and justice.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts answering the question from step 5. The first answer comes from רב יוסף, who sides with רבי אלעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף holds that nothing needs to change during the ten days. The year-round endings are fine. This matches רבי אלעזר's view in steps 3-4.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who here rules like רבי אלעזר

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
'The holy God' and 'King Who loves righteousness and justice.'
phrases.notes: These are the regular year-round endings.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: First answer to the question of which view is the הלכה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which view is the הלכה: רב or רבי אלעזר
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב יוסף: keep the regular endings, like רבי אלעזר

steps.title: רבה changes the endings
steps.stepSummary: רבה rules that we say הַמֶּלֶךְ הַקָּדוֹשׁ and הַמֶּלֶךְ הַמִּשְׁפָּט, following רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: We say 'The holy King' and 'The King of justice.'
steps.whatsHappening: A second אמורא answers differently. רבה sides with רב and says the endings must change during the ten days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the old disagreement between רב and רבי אלעזר is carried on by רב יוסף and רבה. רבה holds that the ten days call for the special 'King' wording.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who here rules like רב
The King of justice, the special ending for the ten days

phrases.english: Rabba said:
'The holy King' and 'The King of justice.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רב יוסף
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבה: change the endings, like רב

steps.title: The הלכה follows רבה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rules that the הלכה follows רבה. We change the endings during the ten days.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה is like רבה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final ruling. We follow רבה and say הַמֶּלֶךְ הַקָּדוֹשׁ and הַמֶּלֶךְ הַמִּשְׁפָּט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This settles the question from step 5. Since רבה follows רב, the practical הלכה is like רב: the endings change from ראש השנה to יום כפור.
steps.whatToRemember: During the ten days of תשובה we say הַמֶּלֶךְ הַקָּדוֹשׁ and הַמֶּלֶךְ הַמִּשְׁפָּט, because the הלכה follows רבה, who follows רב.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the changes we make in שמונה עשרה every year between ראש השנה and יום כפור.

phrases.english: And the halakha is like Rabba.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides between רב יוסף and רבה
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The endings change during the ten days, like רבה and רב

steps.title: Not praying for others is a sin
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר חיננא סבא teaches in רב's name that whoever can pray for another person and does not is called a sinner.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבה בר חיננא סבא said in the name of רב: Anyone who is able to ask for mercy for his friend and does not ask is called a 'sinner.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new teaching about prayer. It is also from רב. If you can pray for someone and you do not, that counts as a sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not only a nice extra. Choosing not to pray for someone in need is labeled a sin. The source for this comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: רבה bar Ḥinnana the Elder, who reports רב's teachings
To ask for mercy, meaning to pray

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַבָּה בַּר חִינָּנָא סָבָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב:
phrases.english: And Rabba bar Ḥinnana the Elder said in the name of Rav:

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל שֶׁאֶפְשָׁר לוֹ לְבַקֵּשׁ רַחֲמִים עַל חֲבֵירוֹ
phrases.english: Anyone who is able to ask for mercy for his friend
and does not ask —
is called a 'sinner.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבָּה בַּר חִינָּנָא סָבָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new teaching from the same רב, connected by the theme of prayer
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Someone who can pray for another and does not is called a sinner

steps.title: Proof from שמואל's words
steps.stepSummary: The source is שמואל הנביא, who said that stopping to pray for the people would be a sin against ה׳.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: 'Also I, far be it from me to sin against ה׳ by stopping to pray for you.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the פסוק that shows not praying for others is a sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל calls 'stopping to pray for you' a sin against ה׳. That shows that failing to pray for others, when you are able to, is a real sin.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is said, used to bring a פסוק

phrases.english: As it is said: 'Also I, far be it from me'
phrases.notes: שמואל א יב:כג

phrases.english: to sin against ה׳ by stopping to pray for you.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for step 9
steps.raayaObject: Not praying for others is a sin

steps.title: For a תלמיד חכם, you must worry until sick
steps.stepSummary: רבא adds that if the person in need is a תלמיד חכם, praying is not enough. You must make yourself sick with worry over him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: If he is a תלמיד חכם, one must make himself sick over him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא builds on the last teaching. For a תלמיד חכם, more than prayer is needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 9 required praying for anyone. רבא raises the level for a תלמיד חכם: you must feel his pain so deeply that it affects you physically.

keyTerms.meaning: That he make himself sick, with worry and concern

phrases.english: Rava said:
If he is a Torah scholar,
one must make himself sick over him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a higher standard to step 9 for a תלמיד חכם
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For a תלמיד חכם, one must make himself sick with concern, not only pray

steps.title: What is the source for רבא's rule?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of רבא's rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks where רבא learns this from. This sets up the search for a פסוק in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא gave a rule without a source. The גמרא wants a פסוק that shows we must make ourselves sick over a תלמיד חכם.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason or source?

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of step 11
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A פסוק that supports רבא's rule

steps.title: A suggested proof from שאול המלך
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests a source: שאול complained that none of his men were sick over him.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it is because it is written: 'And none of you is sick over me, and none tells me.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests a possible source. It is only a suggestion, and the next step will reject it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שאול blamed his men for not being 'sick' over him. Since שאול was a תלמיד חכם, this could show that people should feel sick over a תלמיד חכם.

keyTerms.meaning: If you will say, introducing a suggestion that will be rejected
And none of you is sick over me

steps.confusionAlert: The word אִילֵּימָא signals a proof that the גמרא is about to reject. Do not treat this פסוק as the final source.

phrases.english: If you say it is because it is written:
'And none of you is sick over me'
phrases.notes: שמואל א כב:ח, said by שאול

phrases.english: and none tells me' —

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a first answer to the question in step 12
steps.raayaObject: One must be sick over a תלמיד חכם

steps.title: A king may be different
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. Maybe a king deserves this extra concern, but an ordinary תלמיד חכם does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps a king is different.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the proof from שאול. It may only teach a rule about a king.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שאול was a king, not only a תלמיד חכם. The extra concern may be because of his royal status, so the פסוק does not prove רבא's rule.

phrases.english: Perhaps a king is different.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof in step 13
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from שאול, not רבא's rule
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The פסוק is about a king, so it may not apply to an ordinary תלמיד חכם

steps.title: The real source: דוד wore sackcloth
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a better source. דוד wore sackcloth when דואג and אחיתופל, who were תלמידי חכמים, were sick.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is from here: 'But as for me, when they were sick, my clothing was sackcloth, etc.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its final source for רבא's rule. It uses a פסוק from תהלים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: דוד was talking about his enemies, דואג and אחיתופל. They were not kings, but they were תלמידי חכמים. Even so, דוד wore sackcloth and fasted when they were sick. This avoids the 'king is different' problem.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, from here, bringing a better source

steps.whatToRemember: We must pray for anyone in need. For a תלמיד חכם, we must care so much that it affects us, like דוד, who wore sackcloth and fasted.

phrases.english: Rather, from here:
'But as for me, when they were sick, my clothing was [sackcloth], etc.'
phrases.notes: תהלים לה:יג. The verse goes on: 'I afflicted my soul with fasting.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected proof with a stronger one
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The source is תהלים לה:יג: דוד wore sackcloth for sick תלמידי חכמים who were not kings

steps.title: Being ashamed of a sin brings forgiveness for all sins
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר חיננא סבא, quoting רב, teaches that a person who sins and feels ashamed of it is forgiven for all his sins. The source is a פסוק in יחזקאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבה בר חיננא סבא said in the name of רב: Anyone who does a sin and is ashamed of it is forgiven for all his sins. As it says: 'So that you will remember and be ashamed, and you will never again open your mouth because of your shame, when I forgive you for all that you have done, says ה׳ God.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a brand-new teaching: real shame over a sin leads to complete forgiveness. It backs this up with a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the פסוק, shame ('ובשת', 'כלמתך') appears right next to forgiveness ('בכפרי לך לכל אשר עשית'). רב reads this as cause and effect: the shame is what brings the forgiveness, and it covers ALL sins, not just the one that caused the shame.

keyTerms.meaning: an 'opening of the mouth', meaning a reason to speak up or defend oneself

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how powerful real shame is in תשובה. Feeling embarrassed about a sin is not just a bad feeling. It can actually wipe the slate clean.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַבָּה בַּר חִינָּנָא סָבָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב:
phrases.english: And Rabbah bar Chinnana the Elder said in the name of Rav:
Anyone who does a sinful act
and is ashamed of it
they forgive him for all his sins.
As it says: "So that you will remember and be ashamed,
phrases.notes: יחזקאל 16:63. The prophet is speaking to the Jewish people as a whole.

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא יִהְיֶה לָּךְ עוֹד פִּתְחוֹן פֶּה
phrases.english: and you will never again have an opening of the mouth
because of your shame,
when I forgive you for all that you have done,
says the Lord God."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבָּה בַּר חִינָּנָא סָבָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new teaching by the same author. It is not connected to the topic of praying for a תלמיד חכם in steps 11-15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person who sins and is ashamed of it is forgiven for all his sins.

steps.title: Maybe a whole community is different
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof from יחזקאל. That פסוק talks to the whole Jewish people, and a community may get forgiveness more easily than one person.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps a community is different.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof it just brought. The פסוק in יחזקאל is about the whole nation, so it may not teach anything about a single person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A צבור (community) has special power to be forgiven, more than any one individual. So the פסוק might only show that a community's shame brings forgiveness. It does not prove רב's rule for a regular individual.
steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying רב's rule is wrong. It is only saying this particular פסוק may not prove it for an individual. The rule itself still stands, and the גמרא goes looking for a better source.

phrases.english: Perhaps a community is different.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 16.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof from the פסוק in יחזקאל is rejected. רב's rule itself is not rejected.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The פסוק is about a צבור, which may have a special power to be forgiven that a single person does not have.

steps.title: A new proof from שאול, who did not mention the אורים ותומים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a proof about one person, שאול. When שאול lists the ways he tried to reach ה׳, he names prophets and dreams but leaves out the אורים ותומים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the proof is from here: 'And שמואל said to שאול, Why have you disturbed me by bringing me up? And שאול said, I am in great distress. The Philistines are fighting against me, and God has turned away from me and no longer answers me, not through the prophets and not through dreams. So I have called you to tell me what to do.' But he did not mention the אורים ותומים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new proof that is about a single person, שאול המלך. It notices that שאול leaves out the אורים ותומים, and this sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the פסוק says שאול asked ה׳ through dreams, אורים, and prophets. Yet when he speaks to שמואל, he leaves out the אורים. The גמרא treats this gap as a clue: something stopped שאול from even mentioning it.

keyTerms.meaning: the stones in the כהן גדול's breastplate, used to ask ה׳ questions

phrases.english: Rather, from here:
"And Samuel said to Saul:
phrases.notes: שמואל א 28:15. שאול had a necromancer bring up שמואל after שמואל's death.

phrases.english: Why have you disturbed me by bringing me up?
And Saul said: I am in great distress,
and the Philistines are fighting against me,

phrases.aramaic: וַה׳ סָר מֵעָלַי וְלֹא עָנָנִי עוֹד
phrases.english: and God has turned away from me and no longer answers me,
neither through the prophets nor through dreams,
so I have called you
to tell me what I should do."
But "Urim and Tummim" he did not say.
phrases.notes: שמואל א 28:6 says שאול asked through dreams, אורים, and prophets. Here he leaves the אורים out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the proof that was rejected in step 17 with a proof about an individual.
steps.raayaObject: רב's rule that shame over a sin brings forgiveness, now shown for an individual.
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמואל א 28:15, where שאול leaves out the אורים ותומים when speaking to שמואל.

steps.title: Why שאול was ashamed: he had killed the כהנים of נוב
steps.stepSummary: שאול left out the אורים ותומים because he had killed the city of כהנים, נוב. He was too ashamed to ask ה׳ through a כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because he had killed Nov, the city of the כהנים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why שאול did not mention the אורים ותומים. He had destroyed נוב, the city of כהנים, so he was ashamed to use something that only a כהן could operate.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The אורים ותומים were worn and used by the כהן גדול. After שאול killed the כהנים of נוב, facing a כהן for help made him feel deep shame. So his silence about the אורים is evidence that he truly felt ashamed of his sin.

keyTerms.meaning: נוב, the city of the כהנים

phrases.english: Because he had killed Nov, the city of the priests.
phrases.notes: See שמואל א chapter 22.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the unspoken question from step 18: why did שאול leave out the אורים ותומים?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: שאול was ashamed to ask through a כהן because he had killed the כהנים of נוב, so his silence shows his shame.

steps.title: How do we know שאול was forgiven?
steps.stepSummary: We have shown that שאול was ashamed. Now the גמרא asks for proof that Heaven actually forgave him.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from where do we know that he was forgiven by Heaven?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the second half of the proof. Showing שאול was ashamed is not enough; we also need to show he was forgiven. This question sets up the final answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To prove רב's rule, the גמרא needs both parts: the shame and the forgiveness. Step 19 proved the shame. This step asks for the forgiveness.

phrases.english: And from where do we know that he was forgiven by Heaven?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from proving שאול's shame (step 19) to asking for proof of his forgiveness.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that שאול was actually forgiven by Heaven.

steps.title: 'With me' means in שמואל's place in Heaven
steps.stepSummary: שמואל told שאול, 'Tomorrow you and your sons will be with me.' רבי יוחנן explains that 'with me' means in שמואל's own section in Heaven, so שאול was forgiven.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: 'And שמואל said to שאול: Tomorrow you and your sons will be with me.' And רבי יוחנן said: 'With me' means in my section.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. שאול will be in the same place in Heaven as the righteous נביא שמואל, which shows his sins were forgiven. This completes the proof of רב's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On the simple level, 'with me' could just mean 'you will die tomorrow.' רבי יוחנן reads it as 'in my מחיצה', meaning שאול will share שמואל's place among the righteous. That could only happen if שאול was forgiven, so we see that his shame led to forgiveness.

keyTerms.meaning: in my section, in my place (in Heaven)

steps.whatToRemember: רב teaches that real shame over a sin brings forgiveness for all sins. The פסוק in יחזקאל was pushed aside because it might only apply to a צבור. The proof for an individual is שאול: he was too ashamed to use the אורים ותומים after killing the כהנים of נוב, and he was forgiven, because he would be 'with' שמואל in Heaven.

phrases.english: As it says: "And Samuel said to Saul:
phrases.notes: שמואל א 28:19

phrases.english: And tomorrow you and your sons will be with me."
phrases.notes: The brackets show a text correction: the version printed in the גמרא has 'מחר', and the actual פסוק reads 'ומחר'.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said:
"With me" means in my section.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר וַיֹּאמֶר שְׁמוּאֵל אֶל שָׁאוּל וּמָחָר אַתָּה וּבָנֶיךָ עִמִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question asked in step 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: שמואל's words 'with me', read by רבי יוחנן as 'in my section', show that שאול was forgiven and would share שמואל's place in Heaven.

steps.title: The רבנן prove שאול was forgiven from the words 'chosen of ה׳'
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן offer a different proof that שאול was forgiven. In a פסוק, the people of גבעון speak about 'שאול, the chosen of ה׳.' The רבנן say a בת קול added those last words.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן say the proof comes from here: 'We will hang them up to ה׳ in the Giv'ah of שאול, the chosen of ה׳.' A בת קול came out and said 'the chosen of ה׳.'
steps.whatsHappening: The רבנן give a second answer to the question from Step 20: how do we know Heaven forgave שאול? They point to a פסוק that calls him 'the chosen of ה׳.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The people of גבעון hated שאול, so they would never call him 'chosen of ה׳.' This shows those words came from a בת קול, a voice from Heaven. If Heaven itself calls שאול 'chosen,' then he must have been forgiven.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages, the majority of the חכמים
From here, meaning from this source
And we will hang them up

steps.whatToRemember: There are two proofs that שאול was forgiven. רבי יוחנן learns it from 'with me' (in שמואל's section of Heaven). The רבנן learn it from the בת קול that called him 'chosen of ה׳.'
steps.confusionAlert: The words 'chosen of ה׳' sit inside the speech of the people of גבעון, but the רבנן say those people did not say them. A בת קול said them.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis say: from here
phrases.notes: An alternative source to רבי יוחנן's proof.

phrases.english: 'And we will hang them up to ה׳
phrases.notes: Spoken by the people of גבעון to דוד (שמואל ב כא:ו).

phrases.english: in the Giv'ah of Shaul, the chosen of ה׳.'
phrases.notes: The people of גבעון would not praise שאול like this.

phrases.english: A heavenly voice came out and said 'the chosen of ה׳.'
phrases.notes: Heaven calls שאול chosen, so he was forgiven.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer, parallel to רבי יוחנן's answer in Step 21, to the question in Step 20.
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמואל ב כא:ו, 'בחיר ה׳', read as the words of a בת קול
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A בת קול called שאול 'chosen of ה׳,' which shows he was forgiven.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: שאול was forgiven, whether we learn it from רבי יוחנן's proof or the רבנן's proof.

steps.title: The חכמים wanted to add פרשת בלק to קריאת שמע but did not
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to קריאת שמע. רבי אבהו בן זוטרתי, quoting רבי יהודה בר זבידא, says the חכמים wanted to add פרשת בלק to קריאת שמע. They decided not to because it would be too much of a burden on the people.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו בן זוטרתי said in the name of רבי יהודה בר זבידא: They wanted to set פרשת בלק into קריאת שמע. Why didn't they? Because of the burden on the community.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא leaves the story of שאול and goes back to the chapter's main topic, קריאת שמע. It reports that the חכמים once planned to add פרשת בלק to שמע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים saw something valuable in פרשת בלק and wanted it said every day. They held back only because פרשת בלק is long, and asking the people to say it twice a day would be a טורח ציבור. This sets up the next question: what made פרשת בלק so special?

keyTerms.meaning: To set it as a fixed part
The Torah section about בלק and the blessings of בלעם
The reading of שמע, said every morning and night

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a general rule: the חכמים weighed spiritual benefit against how much they could fairly ask the people to do.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu ben Zutarti said
Rabbi Yehuda bar Zevida said:
phrases.notes: He is the original source of the teaching.

phrases.english: They sought to establish the portion of Balak
in the recitation of Shema,
and why did they not establish it?
Because of the burden on the community.
phrases.notes: פרשת בלק is long.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ בֶּן זוּטַרְתִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בַּר זְבִידָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic. The גמרא returns from the שאול story to קריאת שמע.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The חכמים wanted to add פרשת בלק to קריאת שמע but did not, because of טורח ציבור.

steps.title: Why did they want פרשת בלק? A first guess: it mentions leaving Egypt
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the חכמים wanted פרשת בלק in the first place. It suggests that the reason is that the פרשה mentions יציאת מצרים.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? If you say it is because it is written there, 'ה׳ who brings them out of Egypt'...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the חכמים' wish to add פרשת בלק. It offers a first guess, which it is setting up to test in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We are required to mention יציאת מצרים in קריאת שמע, so a פרשה that mentions it seems like a good fit. The word 'אילימא' ('if you say') is a signal that this guess will probably be rejected.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (a guess that will likely be rejected)
ה׳ who brings them out of Egypt

phrases.english: What is the reason?
phrases.notes: Why did they want this פרשה at all?

phrases.english: If you say it is because it is written in it:
'God, who brings them out of Egypt'
phrases.notes: במדבר כג:כב, which mentions יציאת מצרים.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא? אִילֵּימָא מִשּׁוּם דִּכְתִיב בָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the חכמים' plan in Step 23.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What made פרשת בלק worth adding to קריאת שמע?

steps.title: Other short פרשיות also mention יציאת מצרים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the first guess. פרשת רבית and פרשת משקלות also mention יציאת מצרים, so why not add one of those instead?
steps.simpleTranslation: Then let them say the section about interest, or the section about weights, where יציאת מצרים is also written.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the first guess cannot be right. Mentioning יציאת מצרים is not special to פרשת בלק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If יציאת מצרים were the reason, the חכמים could have chosen פרשת רבית or פרשת משקלות. Both mention יציאת מצרים, and both are short, so they would not be a טורח ציבור. Since the חכמים still wanted פרשת בלק specifically, there must be a different reason.

keyTerms.meaning: The section about lending with interest

phrases.english: Let them say the portion of interest
phrases.notes: ויקרא כה:לה-לח

phrases.english: or the portion of weights
phrases.notes: ויקרא יט:לה-לז

phrases.english: since the exodus from Egypt is written in them.
phrases.notes: These are also short, so they are no burden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the guess offered in Step 24.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the suggested reason (יציאת מצרים), not the fact that the חכמים wanted פרשת בלק
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The suggested reason is not unique to פרשת בלק, and shorter פרשיות would do the same job.
steps.kashyaTarget: The guess that יציאת מצרים was the reason
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If that were the reason, shorter parshiyos would have been chosen.

steps.title: The real reason: a פסוק about lying down and rising up
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי בר אבין gives the true reason. פרשת בלק contains the פסוק 'He crouched, lay down like a lion... who will raise him up?' This matches the words of שמע, 'when you lie down and when you rise up.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבי יוסי בר אבין said: It is because this פסוק is written in it: 'He crouched, he lay down like a lion and like a lioness, who will raise him up?'
steps.whatsHappening: After rejecting the first guess, the גמרא gives the real reason, from רבי יוסי בר אבין. One special פסוק in פרשת בלק explains why the חכמים wanted it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק speaks of lying down and getting up, just like 'ובשכבך ובקומך' in שמע. No short פרשה has this theme, so only פרשת בלק could provide it. Still, the פרשה was too long, so the plan was dropped because of טורח ציבור.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (rejects the earlier idea and brings a new one)
Like a lion and like a lioness

steps.whatToRemember: The חכמים wanted פרשת בלק in שמע because of the פסוק 'כרע שכב... מי יקימנו,' which echoes 'בשכבך ובקומך.' They did not add it because the פרשה is long, which would be a טורח ציבור.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר אָבִין,
phrases.english: Rather, Rabbi Yosei bar Avin said:
Because this verse is written in it:
'He crouched, he lay down like a lion
phrases.notes: במדבר כד:ט. 'Lay down' matches 'בשכבך.'

phrases.english: and like a lioness; who will raise him up?'
phrases.notes: 'Raise up' matches 'ובקומך.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר אָבִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected guess from Steps 24 and 25 with the true reason.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: פרשת בלק contains a פסוק about lying down and rising, which matches the theme of שמע.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The draw of פרשת בלק was the פסוק 'כרע שכב... מי יקימנו.'

steps.title: Why not say just the one lion verse?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the previous answer. If the only reason for פרשת בלק is one פסוק, we could say that פסוק alone.
steps.simpleTranslation: And let us say just this verse and nothing more.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רבי יוסי בר אבין's reason. If one פסוק is the point, why not add only that פסוק to קריאת שמע and skip the rest of the פרשה?
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 23, the חכמים said all of פרשת בלק would be too much of a burden (טורח ציבור). But step 26 showed that only one פסוק is the reason. So the burden problem seems easy to solve: just say that one פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: And let him say / let us say

phrases.english: And let us say this verse
phrases.notes: This is the פסוק 'כרע שכב כארי' from step 26.

phrases.english: and nothing more.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the practical result of the reason given in step 26.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the burden of the whole parsha was the only thing stopping the חכמים from adding פרשת בלק.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If one פסוק carries the whole reason, reciting only that פסוק gets the benefit without the burden.

steps.title: We may only read sections the way משה divided them
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers with a tradition: we may only read a Torah section as its own unit if משה רבינו made it a separate section.
steps.simpleTranslation: We have a tradition: any section that משה רבינו divided off, we may divide off. A section that משה רבינו did not divide off, we may not divide off.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge with a tradition. We cannot cut a single פסוק out of the middle of a section to read it alone, because משה רבינו did not make it a separate unit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah is written with breaks between sections (פרשיות פתוחות and סתומות), and these breaks come from משה. The lion פסוק sits inside a larger section, so it cannot be read alone. That leaves two choices: the whole section, which is too heavy a burden, or nothing. So the חכמים chose nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: We have a tradition (passed down, not derived from a פסוק)
He divided it / set it off as its own section
We divide / we may read it as a separate unit

steps.confusionAlert: 'פסק' here does not mean 'to rule on a הלכה.' It means to cut off or divide a section, as in the breaks between פרשיות in a ספר תורה.
steps.whatToRemember: פרשת בלק was left out because only the whole section could be said. A single פסוק cannot be pulled out of a section that משה רבינו did not divide, and the whole section was too much of a burden on the people.

phrases.english: We have a tradition: any section
phrases.notes: גמירי means a received tradition.

phrases.english: that Moshe our teacher divided off, we may divide off,

phrases.aramaic: דְּלָא פַּסְקַהּ מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ — לָא פָּסְקִינַן.
phrases.english: one that Moshe our teacher did not divide off, we may not divide off.
phrases.notes: The lion פסוק is in the middle of a section, so it cannot be read alone.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 27.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Cites a received tradition that rules out the suggested shortcut.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We could simply say the one important פסוק and avoid the burden.
steps.terutzMaskana: We may not cut a פסוק out of a section that משה did not divide. So it had to be all of פרשת בלק or nothing, and the burden made it nothing.

steps.title: Why was the section of ציצית made part of קריאת שמע?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא moves on and asks why פרשת ציצית was chosen as part of קריאת שמע.
steps.simpleTranslation: The section of ציצית, for what reason did they establish it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question about the third section of קריאת שמע. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first two sections of שמע deal with accepting ה׳ and His מצוות‎. פרשת ציצית seems to be about one specific מצוה. So the גמרא wants to know what earned it a place in the daily קריאת שמע.

keyTerms.meaning: The Torah section about ציצית (במדבר ט״ו), the third section of שמע
They established it (as a fixed part of the recitation)

phrases.english: The section of tzitzis,
for what reason did they establish it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After explaining why פרשת בלק was not added, the גמרא asks why פרשת ציצית was added.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason פרשת ציצית became a fixed part of קריאת שמע.

steps.title: פרשת ציצית contains several key themes
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה בר חביבא explains that פרשת ציצית contains several important ideas, including יציאת מצרים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה בר חביבא said: Because it contains five things: the מצוה of ציצית, the Exodus from Egypt, the yoke of the מצוות, the beliefs of heretics, thoughts of sin, and thoughts of idol worship.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה בר חביבא answers the question. פרשת ציצית was chosen because it holds a whole list of important ideas that are worth saying every day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Besides the מצוה of ציצית itself, the parsha mentions יציאת מצרים. The מפרשים point to this as the main reason, since we must remember the Exodus every day. steps.title: Three ideas are explicit; where are the other three?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts that עול מצות, ציצית, and יציאת מצרים are stated openly in פרשת ציצית. It then asks where the other three ideas, heresy, sinful thoughts, and thoughts of idolatry, are found.
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted, these three are stated openly. The yoke of מצוות: as it is written, 'And you shall see it and remember all the מצוות of ה׳.' Tzitzis: as it is written, 'And they shall make for themselves tzitzis.' The Exodus from Egypt: as it is written, 'Who took you out.' But heresy, sinful thoughts, and thoughts of idolatry: where do we learn them from?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא checks the list of six ideas that רבי יהודה בר חביבא said are in פרשת ציצית. Three are easy to find in the פסוקים, so it asks where the other three come from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 30 listed six ideas. The גמרא now matches each one to a פסוק. Three match plainly, but nothing in the פרשה openly says 'heresy,' 'sinful thoughts,' or 'idolatry,' so a source is needed.

steps.title: A ברייתא finds the three hidden ideas in the פסוק
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא reads 'after your hearts' as heresy, 'after your eyes' as sinful thoughts, and 'you stray' as idolatry. Each reading is backed up by another פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: 'After your hearts' means heresy, as it says, 'The fool said in his heart, there is no God.' 'After your eyes' means sinful thoughts, as it says, 'שמשון said to his father, take her for me, for she is right in my eyes.' 'You stray' means thoughts of idolatry, as it says, 'And they strayed after the Baalim.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא. It shows that three phrases in the פסוק 'do not stray after your hearts and after your eyes' each hint at one of the missing ideas.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each phrase is linked to its meaning through a matching word in another פסוק. 'Heart' links to the fool who denies God in his heart. 'Eyes' links to שמשון choosing a wife by sight. 'Straying' (זנות) links to the נביאים, who use that word for idolatry. So all six ideas really are in פרשת ציצית.

steps.title: New משנה: we mention the Exodus at night
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה rules that יציאת מצרים is mentioned at night, not only during the day.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: We mention the Exodus from Egypt at night.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It rules that the מצוה to mention יציאת מצרים applies at night too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This connects to what came just before. פרשת ציצית holds the mention of יציאת מצרים, but ציצית itself is a daytime מצוה. So one might think the Exodus is only mentioned by day. The משנה rules that it is mentioned at night as well.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה (opening of a new משנה)

steps.confusionAlert: The משנה is talking about mentioning יציאת מצרים at night. It is not making a new rule about the time for קריאת שמע itself.

phrases.english: Mishnah: We mention the Exodus from Egypt at night.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה. The topic follows naturally from יציאת מצרים in פרשת ציצית.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: יציאת מצרים is mentioned at night as well as by day.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה could not prove it until בן זומא
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה says that despite being like a seventy-year-old, he could never prove the night mention until בן זומא derived it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה said: I am like a seventy-year-old, and I did not succeed in having the Exodus mentioned at night, until בן זומא derived it from a verse.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה adds a personal statement. He had wanted to show that the Exodus must be mentioned at night but could not prove it, until בן זומא gave a דרשה. This sets up the next step, where the דרשה is quoted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He tells us the rule in the משנה was not obvious. Even a great, respected scholar could not establish it on his own. The proof came from בן זומא's reading of a פסוק, which we are about to see.

keyTerms.meaning: He derived it from the פסוק by exposition

steps.confusionAlert: Notice the word 'כ' (like). He was not actually seventy; he only looked and was treated like an old man. According to the גמרא elsewhere, he was young and his hair miraculously turned white when he was appointed.

steps.title: בן זומא's proof from the extra word 'כל'
steps.stepSummary: בן זומא reads 'the days of your life' as the daytime, and the extra word 'all' as adding the nights.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: 'So that you remember the day you left the land of Egypt all the days of your life.' 'The days of your life' means the days. 'All the days of your life' adds the nights.
steps.whatsHappening: Here is בן זומא's דרשה. He uses the extra word 'כל' in the פסוק to prove that the Exodus must be remembered at night too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'the days of your life' alone would already mean every day. So the word 'all' must be adding something more, namely the nights. This is the source for the משנה's ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: All the days of your life

steps.whyThisMatters: This דרשה is the source for mentioning יציאת מצרים at night. It is also the famous passage quoted in the הגדה של פסח.

steps.title: The חכמים read 'all' as adding the days of the משיח
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים say 'ימי חייך' means this world, and the extra word 'כל' comes to include the days of the משיח.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the חכמים say: 'The days of your life' means this world. 'All' comes to include the days of the משיח.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the חכמים's own reading of the same פסוק בן זומא used. They use the extra word 'כל' to add something different from what he added.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בן זומא used 'כל' to add the nights. The חכמים use 'כל' to add a future time period, the days of the משיח. So the same extra word is used for two different things, and the חכמים do not get a nighttime obligation from this פסוק.
steps.confusionAlert: Both sides agree that 'כל' adds something. They only disagree about WHAT it adds: nights (בן זומא) or the days of the משיח (חכמים).

phrases.english: And the Sages say:

steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'כל ימי חייך' covers this world and the days of the משיח. There is no source here for mentioning יציאת מצרים at night.

steps.title: בן זומא: Will יציאת מצרים even be mentioned in the days of the משיח?
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא records בן זומא challenging the חכמים with a פסוק in ירמיהו. It says that in the future people will no longer mention יציאת מצרים.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: בן זומא said to the Sages: Do we really mention the Exodus from Egypt in the days of the Messiah? Doesn't the פסוק say: 'Behold, days are coming, says ה׳, when they will no longer say: As ה׳ lives, Who brought up the children of Israel from the land of Egypt. Rather: As ה׳ lives, Who brought up and Who led the descendants of the house of Israel from the northern land and from all the lands where I scattered them.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and quotes a ברייתא. In it, בן זומא attacks the חכמים's reading by showing a פסוק that seems to say יציאת מצרים will stop being mentioned in the days of the משיח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים said 'כל' adds the days of the משיח, so יציאת מצרים will be mentioned then. But ירמיהו says 'they will no longer say' the line about leaving Egypt. They will praise ה׳ for the later gathering of the exiles instead. If so, how can the תורה include the days of the משיח in a מצוה to mention יציאת מצרים?

steps.title: The Exodus will not be erased, only made secondary
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים answer that the פסוק does not mean יציאת מצרים will be forgotten. It means the redemption from the later exiles will be the main thing, and יציאת מצרים will be secondary.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: It does not mean that the Exodus from Egypt will be uprooted from its place. Rather, the redemption from the rule of the nations will be the main thing, and the Exodus from Egypt will be secondary to it.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים answer בן זומא by explaining the פסוק in ירמיהו differently. 'They will no longer say' does not mean 'never again.' It means it will no longer be the main topic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים say the words 'they will no longer say' are not absolute. In the future, the main praise will be for being freed from the nations. יציאת מצרים will still be mentioned, only as the lesser part. So the days of the משיח can still be included in the מצוה.

keyTerms.meaning: That it will be uprooted, totally removed

steps.title: A parallel case: יעקב's name becoming ישראל
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים start bringing a similar case, the פסוק saying יעקב's name will no longer be יעקב, but ישראל. That also uses 'no longer' without meaning total removal.
steps.simpleTranslation: In a similar way you say: 'Your name will no longer be called יעקב, but ישראל will be your name.'
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים set up a proof for their answer by quoting a parallel פסוק. The explanation of this פסוק continues in the next part of the גמרא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says 'no longer' about the name יעקב, yet the name יעקב is still used afterward. This shows that 'no longer' in a פסוק can mean 'no longer the main one' and not 'gone entirely.' This supports the חכמים's reading of the פסוק in ירמיהו.
